Access ALITA

ALITA runs online, protected by Cloudflare. The research team logs in with an e-mail code, peer reviewers with an invitation code. No password, no installation.

RESEARCH TEAM

Dedicated access with your e-mail

At alita.prodigi-marburg.de. Only the research team's e-mail addresses are enabled.

PEER REVIEW

Separate access with an invitation code

Reviewers log in at review.prodigi-marburg.de with the invitation code from the editor. No name or e-mail needed.

Research team: log in in three steps

1

Open ALITA

Open alita.prodigi-marburg.de or the access link you were sent, in any current browser.

2

Enter your e-mail

The page Log in to alita appears. Enter the address that was enabled for you and click Send login code.

3

Enter the code

Cloudflare e-mails you a login code. Enter it on the same page; ALITA opens.

The login page you see in step 2

Peer reviewers: log in with the invitation code

1

Open the reviewer page

review.prodigi-marburg.de/review-login.html

2

Enter the invitation code

Paste the code supplied by the editor into Invitation code and click Continue.

3

Read and download

Reviewers can read and download all documents but cannot change data.

Keep the invitation code confidential; it is sent separately and not printed here. Cloudflare may process connection information such as your IP address; this is not a guarantee of network anonymity.

What you can do once you're in

Without an OpenRouter key

Look around:

  • Knowledge map, clusters and the 3D view
  • Documents list and document details
  • Release notes and documentation

With an OpenRouter key with credit

Everything that uses the language model:

  • Ask questions in Document Chat and Graph Chat
  • Upload documents with summaries

Remember: each user needs their own key, reviewers too. How to get one → page 2

No login code arriving? (research team)

  • Check your spam folder and wait a minute.
  • Use exactly the address that was enabled; other addresses get no access.
  • Still nothing? Ask the ALITA team to enable your address.

ALITA · FRONT-END v2.2.0 · PAGE 2

Get an OpenRouter API key

ALITA answers through OpenRouter. You need your own key once; it takes about five minutes.

1

Create an account

Go to openrouter.ai and click Sign in. Sign up with Google, GitHub or your e-mail address.

2

Add credits

Open openrouter.ai/settings/credits and buy credits. OpenRouter works prepaid: requests are paid from this balance.

  • Payment by credit card, AliPay or USDC. Card payments carry a 5.5% fee (at least $0.80).
  • Starting with €5 is fine. At about €0.003 per 10-page paper and well under one cent per question, that lasts for hundreds of questions and uploads.
  • Unused credits can be refunded within 24 hours of purchase. Optional: auto top-up refills the balance below a threshold you set.
Why credits?ALITA uses a paid model. Free models exist on OpenRouter but are limited to 50 requests per day without purchased credits.
3

Create the key

Open openrouter.ai/settings/keys and click Create Key.

  • Name: for example ALITA, so you recognise it later.
  • Credit limit: set a limit (for example $10) or choose no limit. Once the limit is reached, requests with this key are rejected until you raise it.
  • Copy the key right away. It starts with sk-or- and is shown only once.
4

Paste it into ALITA

In the top bar, paste the key into OpenRouter API-Key and click Save. The status changes from no key to Key … with its last four characters. The key is stored in this browser; on another device or browser, enter it again.

5

Keep it safe

  • Treat the key like a password: don't share it, put it in e-mails or commit it to Git.
  • Lost or leaked? Delete it under openrouter.ai/settings/keys and create a new one. OpenRouter also e-mails you if it detects an exposed key.
  • Check your usage and balance any time under Activity and Credits in your OpenRouter account.

Checklist

Account created
Credits added
Key copied
Saved in ALITA

Fees and limits as stated by OpenRouter, October 2026; they can change. Sources: openrouter.ai/docs/faq · openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/authentication

Quick Reference

Ask your research documents and get answers with sources you can check.

A · DOCUMENT CHAT What do the documents say?
B · GRAPH CHAT How are people, projects and methods connected?

Get started three steps, once

1

Open ALITA

Log in with your e-mail and code (page 1). Pick a view in the top bar: B or A/B.

2

Enter your API key

Paste your OpenRouter key (sk-or-v1-…) and click Save. The browser keeps it. No key yet? How to get one → page 2

3

Choose databases

Click one or more databases. No selection searches all of them. The choice applies to both chats.

Ask a question pick the chat that fits the question

ⓘ

Where to find them: the tab A/B Interaction Interface shows both chats side by side. The tab B Interaction Interface shows only Graph Chat (B), next to the knowledge map, so Document Chat (A) is only visible on A/B.

ADocument Chat

RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) searches the text: ALITA has cut every document into short passages; it finds the passages closest in meaning to your question and writes the answer from them. Best for content, details, quotes and summaries. Narrow the scope under Advanced settings (type, method, cluster, years).

Every claim cites its source as [1], [2]. Click a number to see the passage; Copy takes the answer with its sources.

BGraph Chat

GraphRAG searches the connections: on upload, ALITA builds a knowledge graph of people, projects, methods, clusters and document parts, linked by relations such as authored, uses_method or cites. It starts at what your question names and follows these links. Best for relationships: who worked on what, which methods a project uses, who cites whom. The answer shows the path it followed. The graph is based on the SPAR ontologies DoCO, DEO, FaBiO and CiTO plus BIBO for citations between the papers of the collection (page 6).

Under Advanced settings → Parameters: filter by entity, relation and period, and set hops (1–4) for how far the graph is followed.

EXAMPLE QUESTIONS “Who worked with whom on project X?” · more on page 5

Explore and add data

Cluster map and 3D view

Hover a point to preview, click it to open the document. Click a cluster to limit both chats to it. Reset view restores the start view.

3D · time adds the years as depth: W S forward/back, A D sideways, drag to look, Esc to close, or Fly through time.

Add documents

Click + Add new data (or Documents → + Upload). Choose the database, the kind of data, optionally a date, then drop the files and click Upload. Projects go in as a ZIP of the folder; tick Generate summary and methods with the LLM to have them filled in.

Cost: about €0.003 per 10-page paper with the LLM summary (well under one cent; 100 papers ≈ €0.30). Without it, only embeddings: below €0.001. ALITA shows the actual cost after each upload.

Uploading uses your OpenRouter key and credits: set it up → page 2

Estimate: 10 pages ≈ 8,000 tokens of text; summary, section labelling and embeddings ≈ 25,000 tokens; GPT-6 Luna at $0.10 / $0.50 per 1M input / output tokens (OpenRouter, Oct 2026).

Prompt filters

@db:Magnoliaonly this database
@type:paperonly papers (or notes, project)
@year:2019-2021only this period
@cluster:3only this cluster

If something looks wrong

No answerCheck the API key is saved (page 2); loosen the filters.
Too narrowClick Clear selection in the database bar.
Off topicClick + New to start a fresh conversation.
Old chatsHistory reopens them (saved in this browser).

ALITA's answers are generated by a language model and can be wrong. Check every statement against its sources.

Use cases for the research proposal

Typical questions, and what the prototype can answer today. ALITA answers from the documents uploaded to it; external literature is outside the prototype.

Current scope of the prototype

This applies to every row below.

✓Within one research project. Click the project in the map; both chats then answer about that project only.
✕Not yet: between research clusters. No dedicated comparison of one cluster with another.
✕Not yet: on paper level. No questions aimed at one single paper or a set of chosen papers.
Status today: Workswithin one project, possibly once data is uploaded Partlyparts work; scope, input or rules missing Not in prototypeplanned for later
Use caseTypical questionWhat ALITA can do today

Your own projects

1

Summarise your own knowledge progress across projects

“How has my understanding of team mental models developed across my projects since 2015?”

Partly – one project at a time

Progress questions are answered from the knowledge stages of a project (table of 3, 5 or 10 stages linked to the files), but per project, not across projects. The researchers' own projects are not uploaded yet (to be clarified with Michael).

2

Identify knowledge leaps and the reasons for them

“Where did my thinking change significantly between my early and my recent papers – and why?”

Partly – basis to define

Within a project, versions are classified as substantive, rewording, formatting or resubmission. Comparing chosen papers needs paper-level questions (not yet). Open: the basis, e.g. older vs. newer papers of the same authors.

3

Assess projects and project plans against academic standards

“How well does this project plan meet the criteria for a sound research design?”

Partly – standards missing

Technically possible. Needed: the project plans (not submitted yet) and the standards, e.g. guidelines as PDF, which can be built into the glossary.

Questions about a project's data and methods

4

Explain how the analyses were done

“Explain to me how I did the analyses.”

Works – within one project

Draws on the methods extracted from the files and the analysis documents (scripts, outputs, manuscripts) of the selected project, with sources.

5

Derive further research questions and loose ends

“What further research questions could be derived? Where are the loose ends?”

Works – within one project

Answered from the project's limitations, discussion and future-work passages. Not yet across clusters or for one chosen paper.

6

Find other uses for the data

“Can you do anything else with the data?”

Works – within one project

Suggestions based on the project's data files, variables and analyses already done. Combining data across projects or clusters is not yet supported.

7

Uncover research gaps

“Which research gaps remain in the 11-MentalModelProcesses project?”

Works – tested

Answered from the uploaded documents, with sources. Test results: [to be added].

Topics and ideas

8

Summarise the state of knowledge on a topic from external sources

“What is the current state of research on trust in generative AI?”

Not in prototype

External sources were excluded for the initial prototype; answers cover only the uploaded documents. Planned as the Window to the outside (REQ-20).

“Here is my idea: … How strong is it, and how could I improve it?”

Works – idea as text

No ideas submitted yet, but none need uploading: paste the idea into the chat. ALITA relates it to the existing documents and cites them.

10

“What more should I do with the data? Where do I need to look deeper?”

Upload the project (+ Add new data, ZIP), click it in the map so the chat is limited to it, then ask.

Ontologies behind ALITA

ALITA describes every document with the SPAR ontologies for scholarly publishing and stores the result in a knowledge graph (Neo4j). Graph Chat (B) answers along it; both chats filter by it.

The ontologies

OntologyDescribesHow ALITA uses itExamples
DEODiscourse Elements Ontology · deo:

The rhetorical role of a text part: 31 classes

Every passage, section and summary element gets one or more roles, detected from headings (EN/DE) or by the language model.

Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, FutureWork, BibliographicReference

DoCODocument Components Ontology · doco:

The structure of a document; imports DEO and the Pattern Ontology

Documents are split into sections and passages in reading order.

Section, Paragraph, Bibliography

Pattern Ontologypo:

Pure containment structure, the base layer of DoCO

The “contains” links: document → section → passage.

Container, Block

FaBiOFRBR-aligned Bibliographic Ontology · fabio:

The type of a publication

Each document is typed by its kind of data.

JournalArticle (paper), Note (notes), WorkPackage (project material)

CiTOCitation Typing Ontology · cito:

Citations between works

DOIs in a document's bibliography become “cites” links, so papers in the collection that cite each other are connected.

Document cites Work

ALITA's ownproject-specific

Research context not covered by SPAR

People, projects and teams, databases, the methods glossary and the semantic clusters.

Person, Project, Database, Method, Cluster

BIBOBibliographic Ontology · bibo:

Bibliographic description and citations between documents

Each document gets its BIBO type and ordered author list; the reference lists are matched with the papers of the collection (DOI or title), so papers and projects that cite each other are linked. Shown as ⇄ Citations in the knowledge map.

AcademicArticle, authorList, cites

How it fits together: the knowledge graph

Personauthor · team member
ProjectALITA
DatabaseAster … Magnolia
Documentfabio:JournalArticle · Note · WorkPackage · bibo:AcademicArticle
Methodmethods glossary
Clustersemantic cluster
Workcito · by DOI
Summary elementstructured summary
Sectiondoco:Section
Passagedoco:Paragraph (chunk)
DEO classdeo:Methods, deo:Results …
DoCO / DEOFaBiOCiTOBIBOALITA's own Sections, passages and summary elements each link to their DEO roles (has_role).

Where you see it in the interface

  • Discourse element filter in both chats: answer only from, e.g., Methods or Results passages. In Graph Chat it is derived from the question if left empty.
  • Graph path under each Graph Chat answer, e.g. Person → authored → Project → uses_method → Method.
  • Relation filter (authored, uses_method, cites, contains, in_cluster) and hops in Graph Chat.
  • ⇄ Citations in the knowledge map: who cites whom inside the collection; in a document's details, “Cites” and “Cited by”.

Why an ontology

Vector search knows which document a passage comes from. The ontology adds what role it plays in the argument (method, result, limitation …) and how documents relate (authors, methods, citations, clusters). Questions like “Where do the papers discuss limitations?” are then answered along an explicit path instead of by similarity alone.

When each ontology is applied during upload: page 7. Details: tab Technical Documentation › Ontology in ALITA. Source: Constantin, Peroni, Pettifer, Shotton, Vitali (2016): The Document Components Ontology (DoCO). Semantic Web 7, 167–181. Ontologies: purl.org/spar/deo · purl.org/spar/doco · purl.org/spar/fabio · purl.org/spar/cito · purl.org/ontology/bibo

ALITA · FRONT-END v2.2.0 · PAGE 7

How documents get into ALITA

The ingestion pipeline, step by step. The ontology is not applied up front: each passage gets its rhetorical role while it is chunked. Clustering runs on the summaries, not on the passages.

Legend: RULE-BASEDno language model LLMGPT-6 Luna, uses the uploader's OpenRouter key ONTOLOGYSPAR ontologies, see page 6 EMBEDDINGtext → vector
1

Extract RULE-BASED

Text and sections with their headings from PDF, Word, Excel …; metadata: type, date, role, version, duplicates, latest version. Methods are tagged by keyword from the methods glossary.

→
Document recordmetadata, methods; duplicates and files without text stop here (metadata only)
2

Summarise LLMoptional · latest version only

A structured summary per work: purpose, design/methodology, findings, limitations, originality, plus methods, keywords and a title.

→
Structured summary5 fields per paper, note or project
3

Chunk and assign roles RULE-BASEDDoCO · DEO

Passages of 1,200 characters with 200 overlap; the location in the file is kept. Each passage gets its DEO role (Methods, Results, Discussion …) from its section heading, in English or German.

→
Passages with rolese.g. “3 Method” → deo:Methods
4

Label the rest LLMDEO

Passages whose heading gives no role are classified by the language model, at most 60 per document to limit cost.

→
All passages labelledready to be stored
5

Embed EMBEDDING

Every passage becomes a vector, with a short header (type, project, file). Every paper, note and project also gets a summary vector from its title and structured summary.

→
Qdrant · passagesvector + section + DEO role
Qdrant · documents & projectsmetadata + summary vector
6

Build the knowledge graph DoCO · DEO · FaBiO · CiTO · BIBO

Document (typed with FaBiO and BIBO) → sections → passages with their DEO roles; people (ordered author list), project, database, methods, the DOIs cited in the bibliography (CiTO) and, after each upload, the citations between documents of the collection, found in the reference lists by DOI or title (BIBO, no LLM).

→
Neo4j · knowledge graphnodes and relations for Graph Chat
7

Cluster K-MEANSLLM for names

After an upload (once at the end of a batch): k-means with cosine similarity on the summary vectors, one point per paper, note or project; project files inherit their project's cluster. Names and short descriptions by the LLM, map positions by PCA.

→
Clusterswritten to Qdrant and the graph

Who uses what

Document Chat (A) · RAG

Searches the passage vectors in Qdrant. The discourse-element filter narrows to, e.g., Methods or Results passages.

Graph Chat (B) · GraphRAG

First finds a path in the graph (Neo4j), then searches only the passages of the documents on that path.

Knowledge map

Shows the clusters from step 7 and their positions; clicking a cluster limits both chats to it.

Defaults from the backend configuration (ALITA v2.1.0): chunk size 1,200 / overlap 200; summaries for the latest version only; at most 60 LLM-labelled passages per document; clustering automatically after each upload. Code: backend/app/ingest.py, chunking.py, deo.py, graph.py, clustering.py.
